title: Finally Riding the Insane Colnago Y1RS - Time to Upgrade?

takeaways.text: On a 40 km chain gang averaging 38 km/h it felt like one of the fastest bikes he had ridden, but not noticeably quicker than an Aeroad CFR, Madone SLR, Propel, Teammachine or Tarmac on this first proper ride.
In strong crosswinds the bike was pushed around more than a Tarmac or Aeroad, which he put down to the frame shape plus deep wheels; the same wheels felt steadier on his own Colnago C64.

The seat-tube junction gave a fairly smooth ride through the saddle, but on rough roads with 28 mm tyres the ride was firm with plenty of feedback, especially through the bar. He rode his own wheels and tyres, not the supplied Vision wheels with 32 mm tyres.
Despite the unusual frame, the contact points, reach and geometry felt like a normal race bike; he found it a bit heavy but gave no weight.

disclosure: David Arthur rode a test bike that arrived for review (the video does not say from whom) and calls his thoughts unpaid. The description names Assos and Insta360 as channel sponsors and links a camera.
summary: An August 2026 first proper ride of a Colnago Y1Rs test bike on a fast group ride, with impressions of speed, crosswind handling and comfort. He used his own deep wheels and 28 mm tyres, so the ride differs from the stock build, and it is a complete bike rather than the mainland frame kit recorded here.
